questions.prompt: Which opening to a complaint response is most likely to escalate rather than resolve the situation?
choices: 'You called on May 3 about the $35 returned-payment fee on your April 28 payment, which you said hit your account before payday. Here is what we found and what we are doing about it.'
'We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and want you to know that your satisfaction is our top priority. We appreciate your patience as we work to resolve this matter.'
'We pulled the ACH on April 27 instead of April 28, which is our error. We have refunded the $35 fee and corrected the pull date.'
'Thanks for reaching out, Mr. Johnson. We read your email carefully and want to walk through what happened.'
questions.explanation: Generic boilerplate apologies — 'inconvenience,' 'top priority,' 'appreciate your patience' — signal to the borrower that nobody read the complaint. The CFPB and regulators look for exactly this pattern as evidence of non-responsive servicing. The other three openings each reference specifics.

questions.prompt: A draft complaint response includes the sentence: 'This was a clear violation of our agreement with you and likely a violation of federal lending law.' Compliance has not yet reviewed the matter. What is the issue?
choices: No issue — owning the mistake builds trust

The sentence states legal conclusions that are not yours to make. Characterizing something as a violation of an agreement or of federal law is a determination for compliance and counsel, and it creates a written record that can be used against Kapitus in arbitration, litigation, or regulatory action. Remove the legal characterizations and keep the factual acknowledgment
The only problem is the word 'clear' — change it to 'possible'
The sentence is fine as long as you delete the response after sending
questions.explanation: There is real legal daylight between empathetic accountability ('we made a mistake — we pulled the payment a day early') and legal conclusions ('this was a violation of federal lending law'). The first is appropriate; the second is for legal and compliance to determine. AI will produce either column without distinguishing.

questions.prompt: Which type of complaint is the worst candidate for a same-day AI-assisted response?
choices: A borrower asking why a $25 late fee was charged on a payment made one day after the due date
A borrower asking for a copy of the most recent statement
A borrower alleging that their application was declined because of their national origin, in a complaint filed through the CFPB portal
A borrower asking for clarification of an interest-rate change disclosed in last month's statement
questions.explanation: Allegations of discrimination — ECOA, fair-lending — filed through a regulator are the highest-stakes complaint type Kapitus handles. They go to compliance and legal first, with AI drafts attached as a starting point at most. Speed is the wrong instinct here; careful is the only correct speed.
